name: Python
description: Python is a beginner-friendly language with clean syntax, used for web back-ends, automation, data science and AI.

blocks.html:
Introduction to Python

What is Python?

Python is a popular, beginner-friendly programming language. Its code reads almost like English, which is why it is used for web back-ends, data science, automation, AI and teaching.

  • Interpreted: you run code line by line, no separate compile step.
  • Dynamically typed: you do not declare types.
  • Batteries included: a huge standard library comes with it.

Your First Program

Save this as hello.py and run it with python hello.py (or try it in the interactive prompt by typing python).

blocks.code:
# My first Python program
print("Hello, Learning Hub!")
print(2 + 3)
print("Python", "is", "fun")
blocks.output:
Hello, Learning Hub!
5
Python is fun

blocks.html:
• print() shows text on the screen.
  • # starts a comment: Python ignores the rest of the line.
  • Text goes in quotes (single or double).

Indentation Is Part of the Syntax

Other languages use { } to group code. Python uses indentation (4 spaces is the standard). Code with the wrong indentation is an error.

blocks.code:
age = 20
if age >= 18:
    print("Adult")      # indented: inside the if
    print("Can vote")
print("Done")           # not indented: always runs

blocks.html:
The colon : at the end of a line opens a block, and the indented lines below it belong to that block.

Why Learn Python First?

StrengthExample
Short codeA task that takes 10 lines in Java is often 3 in Python
Huge communityLibraries for web (Django, Flask), data (pandas) and AI (PyTorch)
Great for learningYou focus on ideas, not on syntax noise

Variables, Types & Input

Variables

A variable is a name for a value. You create it by assigning with =. There is no type to write: Python works it out.

blocks.code:
name = "Ayesha"
age = 20
height = 1.62
is_student = True

print(name, age, height, is_student)

age = age + 1          # variables can change
print(age)

blocks.html:
• Names use letters, digits and underscores, and cannot start with a digit.
  • Python style is snake_case (student_name).
  • Names are case sensitive: age and Age are different.

Basic Types

TypeExampleMeaning
int42Whole numbers (any size)
float3.14Decimal numbers
str"hello"Text
boolTrue / FalseYes or no
NoneTypeNoneMeans "no value"

Use type(x) to see the type, and int(), float(), str() to convert between types.

blocks.code:
x = 7
print(type(x))
print(type(7.0))
print(type("7"))
print(type(True))
print(int("5") + 3)      # text -> number
print(str(5) + "3")      # number -> text
print(float(2))

blocks.html:
f-strings and Input

An f-string puts values inside text: write f"..." and put variables in { }. To read from the keyboard use input(), which always gives text, so convert it when you need a number.

blocks.code:
name = "Sara"
score = 87.456
print(f"{name} scored {score:.1f}%")
print(f"Double: {score * 2:.2f}")
print(f"{name.upper()} has {len(name)} letters")
blocks.output:
Sara scored 87.5%
Double: 174.91
SARA has 4 letters

blocks.html:
name = input("Your name: ")
age = int(input("Your age: "))      # convert text to a number
print(f"Hello {name}, next year you will be {age + 1}")

Operators & Conditions

Operators

KindOperatorsNotes
Arithmetic+ - * // always gives a float
More arithmetic// % **floor division, remainder, power
Comparison== != < > <= >=give True or False
Logicaland or notcombine conditions
Membershipin not inis something inside a list or text?

blocks.code:
print(7 / 2, 7 // 2, 7 % 2, 2 ** 10)
print(5 > 3, 5 == 5.0, "a" < "b")
print(True and False, True or False, not True)
print("py" in "python", 3 in [1, 2, 3])
blocks.output:
3.5 3 1 1024
True True True
False True False
True True

blocks.html:
if, elif, else

Conditions let your program choose. Python checks from top to bottom and runs only the first matching block.

• Do not forget the colon and the indentation.
  • Use == to compare and = to assign.
  • elif means "else if" (you can have many).

Truthiness

Python treats some values as False in a condition: 0, 0.0, "", [], {} and None. Everything else is True.

blocks.code:
for value in [0, 1, "", "hi", [], [0], None]:
    print(repr(value), "->", "True" if value else "False")
blocks.output:
0 -> False
1 -> True
'' -> False
'hi' -> True
[] -> False
[0] -> True
None -> False

blocks.html:
Loops

for Loops and range()

A for loop repeats code for each item in a sequence. range(n) gives the numbers 0 to n-1.

blocks.output:
Round 0
Round 1
Round 2
P
y
Sum 1..5 = 15

blocks.html:
CallGives
range(5)0, 1, 2, 3, 4
range(2, 6)2, 3, 4, 5
range(0, 10, 3)0, 3, 6, 9

while Loops

A while loop keeps going as long as its condition is True. Make sure something inside changes the condition, or the loop never ends.

blocks.code:
count = 3
while count > 0:
    print("Countdown", count)
    count -= 1
print("Liftoff!")

blocks.html:
break, continue and enumerate

  • break leaves the loop immediately.
  • continue skips to the next round.
  • enumerate(items) gives the index and the item together.

Lists & Tuples

Lists

A list holds many values in order. It is mutable: you can add, remove and change items. Indexing starts at 0 and negative indexes count from the end.

blocks.code:
fruits = ["apple", "mango"]
fruits.append("kiwi")
fruits.insert(0, "banana")
print(fruits)
print(fruits[0], fruits[-1], len(fruits))
fruits.remove("mango")
last = fruits.pop()
print(last, fruits)
fruits[0] = "grape"
print(sorted(fruits))

blocks.html:
MethodWhat it does
append(x)Add to the end
insert(i, x)Add at a position
remove(x)Remove the first x
pop()Remove and return the last item
sort()Sort in place
len(list)How many items

Slicing and Comprehensions

A slice items[start:stop] takes part of a list (stop is not included). A list comprehension builds a new list in one line.

blocks.code:
nums = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
print(nums[1:4])      # index 1 to 3
print(nums[:2], nums[3:])
print(nums[::-1])     # reversed

squares = [n * n for n in range(1, 6)]
big = [n for n in nums if n > 25]
print(squares, big)

blocks.html:
Tuples

A tuple is like a list that cannot change (immutable). Use it for fixed groups such as coordinates. You can unpack it into variables.

blocks.code:
point = (3, 4)
x, y = point               # unpacking
print(x, y, point[0])

try:
    point[0] = 9
except TypeError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

print(len((1, 2, 3)), (1, 2) + (3,))
blocks.output:
3 4 3
Error: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment
3 (1, 2, 3)

blocks.html:
Dictionaries & Sets

Dictionaries

A dictionary stores key: value pairs and finds a value quickly by its key. Keys must be unique.

blocks.code:
student = {"name": "Ali", "age": 20}
student["city"] = "Lahore"          # add
student["age"] = 21                 # change
print(student)
print(student["name"], student.get("phone", "no phone"))

for key, value in student.items():
    print(key, "=", value)

del student["city"]
print("city" in student, len(student))
blocks.output:
{'name': 'Ali', 'age': 21, 'city': 'Lahore'}
Ali no phone
name = Ali
age = 21
city = Lahore
False 2

blocks.html:
• d[key] raises an error if the key is missing; d.get(key, default) does not.
  • d.items() gives (key, value) pairs for looping.
  • key in d checks if a key exists.

Sets

A set holds unique values with no order. It is perfect for removing duplicates and for maths-style operations.

blocks.code:
tags = ["web", "python", "web", "css", "python"]
unique = set(tags)
print(sorted(unique), len(unique))

a = {1, 2, 3, 4}
b = {3, 4, 5}
print(sorted(a | b), sorted(a & b), sorted(a - b))
print(2 in a)

blocks.html:
OperationMeaning
a | bUnion (everything)
a & bIntersection (in both)
a - bIn a but not in b

Choosing the Right Container

NeedUse
Ordered items you will changelist
Fixed group of itemstuple
Look up by a name or iddict
Unique items, fast membership testset

Functions

Defining and Calling

A function is a named block of code you can reuse. Define it with def, send values in as parameters and send a result back with return.

blocks.code:
def square(n):
    """Return n multiplied by itself."""
    return n * n

def greet(name):
    print("Hello,", name)

print(square(7))
result = greet("Sara")
print(result)          # greet returns None

blocks.html:
• A function without return gives back None.
  • Write a short text (docstring) under def to explain what it does.

Default, Keyword and Variable Arguments

• size=1 is a default value used when the caller does not pass one.
  • Call with names (greet(name="Ali")) for clarity.
  • *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple; **kwargs collects extra named ones into a dict.

Scope and lambda

Variables created inside a function are local: they disappear when it ends. A lambda is a tiny one-line function, often used with sorted or map.

blocks.code:
x = "global"

def show():
    x = "local"        # a different variable
    return x

print(show(), x)

words = ["pear", "fig", "banana"]
print(sorted(words, key=lambda w: len(w)))
print(list(map(lambda n: n * 2, [1, 2, 3])))

blocks.html:
Classes & Objects

Classes and Objects

A class is a blueprint; an object is one thing made from it. __init__ runs when an object is created, and self means "this object".

• Variables stored on self are the object's attributes.
  • Functions inside a class are methods. Their first parameter is always self.

Special Methods

Methods with double underscores let your class work with Python features. __str__ controls what print() shows.

Inheritance

A class can inherit from another to reuse its code. The child can add methods or override existing ones. super() calls the parent's version.

blocks.output:
Rex says Woof
Tom says Meow

blocks.html:
Errors & Files

Handling Errors

When something goes wrong Python raises an exception. Catch it with try and except so your program does not crash.

blocks.output:
checked '42'
42
'abc' is not a number
checked 'abc'
None
Error: division by zero

blocks.html:
BlockRuns
tryThe risky code
except XOnly if error type X happened
elseOnly if there was no error
finallyAlways (cleanup)

Raising Your Own Errors

blocks.output:
OK: 25
ValueError: age cannot be negative
TypeError: age must be an integer

blocks.html:
Use raise when your code finds a bad situation. Choose a fitting built-in type like ValueError or TypeError.

Reading and Writing Files

Use with open(...). It closes the file for you, even if an error happens. Modes: "r" read, "w" write (erases), "a" append.

blocks.code:
import json, os, tempfile

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "notes.txt")

with open(path, "w") as f:          # write
    f.write("first line\n")
    f.write("second line\n")

with open(path, "a") as f:          # append
    f.write("third line\n")

with open(path) as f:               # read line by line
    for number, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
        print(number, line.strip())

print(json.dumps({"name": "Ali", "scores": [90, 85]}))

try:
    open("missing.txt")
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("missing.txt does not exist")
blocks.output:
1 first line
2 second line
3 third line
{"name": "Ali", "scores": [90, 85]}
missing.txt does not exist

blocks.html:
• Always handle FileNotFoundError when reading a file that may not exist.
  • Use import to use other modules, for example import json to save data as JSON.
